content.text: XRD shows the trirutile NiSb2O6 phase across a wide range of compositions. I'm now spending my first merit measurement near its stoichiometry.

input.verdict: Support. According to MACE, NiSb2O6 trirutile is on the hull (E_hull = 0), and XRD at indices 21 and 15 best matches it. MEGNet's HSE gap of 0.04 eV is likely an artifact of the magnetic Ni2+ state, so I treat it as uninformative. Index 22 (Sb 0.688) is closest to the phase-pure trirutile stoichiometry, which makes it the first measurement.

I am sampling the opposite end of the composition line from the one measured.

content.text:
I submitted **index 30 (Ni 0.17 / Sb 0.83)** as the best composition, with an EQE of 2.76%. All 3 merit measurements are spent; I used 4 of the 5 XRD measurements.

| Index | Ni / Sb | EQE (%) |
|---|---|---|
| 22 | 0.31 / 0.69 | 0.0054 |
| 28 | 0.19 / 0.81 | 0.016 |
| 30 | 0.17 / 0.83 | 2.76 |

- **What I tried first:** MACE predicts that the NiSb₂O₆ (trirutile) phase is thermodynamically stable (on the convex hull). The XRD at indices 15 and 21 matches it best of the phases I checked, though the fit is only moderate (similarity about 0.52–0.55). So I measured index 22, the candidate closest to that phase's composition, but its EQE was close to zero. MEGNet's band gap of 0.04 eV for this phase looks unreliable, so I didn't use it either way.
- **Why index 30 stands out:** Its XRD has extra peaks beyond the trirutile ones, likely from a second Sb-oxide phase. MACE puts Sb₂O₃ on the hull, so that phase is plausible. It is the only measured sample with meaningful activity.
- **How confident I am:** The good region is very narrow. Index 28, only two steps away, dropped back to 0.016%. Index 30 is the last candidate on the line, so there's nothing further Sb-rich to test. With just three measurements I can't rule out a better spot elsewhere, especially at the Ni-rich end or in the middle (indices 23–27), which I never measured.
